$comment: Audited external versions cited in shipped guidance, and where each is cited.
Two checks run against this file. Coherence (offline, part of `make check`):
every `cited_as` string must still appear in each doc that cites it, so the
manifest cannot drift away from the prose. Freshness (network, nightly):
`audited` is compared against the current upstream release.
`cited_as` exists because `audited` alone is not searchable: a bare major like
"5" matches a numbered step or `Terraform 1.5+`, so guidance could move from v5
to v6 with the manifest still passing. It defaults to `audited` when the version
A `cited_as` item may be {"text": ..., "count": n} to require an exact number of
occurrences, so updating one of several mentions cannot pass while the rest go stale.
`sources` are all machine-readable and readable unauthenticated.
API endpoint paths are deliberately NOT tracked here: HCP Terraform publishes
no machine-readable API schema to diff them against, so any check would be a
hand-maintained second list of the same strings.

entries.name: cf-terraforming
entries.why_it_matters: The per-resource coverage matrix in import.md was written against this release; newer ones may cover more or differ in generated HCL. Cited in four places plus an abbreviated v0.27 claim, all of which must move together.

entries.name: terraform
entries.why_it_matters: Appears in the worked mise.toml a reader copies to establish the toolchain pin.

entries.name: mise-action
entries.why_it_matters: Pinned by commit SHA in the CI example. The SHA is the value that runs; the version is only a comment, so both must move together.

entries.name: cloudflare-provider-major
entries.why_it_matters: Guidance states behaviour specific to the v5 provider; a new major invalidates it.

entries.name: github-provider-major
entries.why_it_matters: Repository, branch-protection and label guidance is written against the v6 provider; a new major invalidates the resource shapes it describes.
